criteria: HRD sector-layer mass at rd >= 4096 sectors >= 0.10
structural_signature_predicate.criteria_provenance: Criterion 4 was originally specified as 'HRD bin-0 mass >= 0.90' in the plan; empirical calibration against sweep_20260514T165947Z_a1closure_ebe60dd showed bin-0 mass is ~0.87 for ALL 4 cells (both admitted slugs AND both negative controls) and therefore does not discriminate the high-footprint signature. The R48 R2 refinement reformulates criterion 4 as 'HRD sector-layer long-rd-tail mass at rd >= 4096 sectors >= 0.10' which DOES discriminate: both admitted slugs show ~12% mass at rd >= 4096 (working set spills beyond L2 cache capacity, forcing long-reuse-distance reuse) while both negative controls show 0% mass at rd >= 4096 (their working sets fit in L2 or smaller). This is the 'low-reuse' half of the 'high-footprint-low-reuse' signature: the absolute reuse-distance tail is the discriminating structural fingerprint, not the bin-0 cold-miss mass. This deviation from the original plan-file criterion (d) for the structural-signature predicate (bin-0 mass >= 0.90) is user-sanctioned via the goal-tracker MUTABLE Plan Evolution Log at .humanize/rlcr/2026-05-20_11-05-10/goal-tracker.md (user-confirmed via in-session AskUserQuestion). The plan file itself stays frozen per BL-20260510-plan-file-frozen-during-active-rlcr-session.
